senses.definition: To cause (a person or animal) to recover from a faint; to cause (a person or animal) to return to a state of consciousness.
To bring (a person or animal which is dead) back to life.
senses.example: And in her cheekes the vermeill red did ſhevv / Like roſes in a bed of lilies ſhed, / The vvhich ambroſiall odours from them threvv, / And gazers ſence vvith double pleaſure fed, / Hable to heale the ſicke, and to reuiue the ded.

senses.definition: To cause (something) to recover from a state of decline, neglect, oblivion, or obscurity; to make (something) active or lively again; to reanimate, to revitalize.
senses.example: The Manx language has been revived after dying out, and is now taught in some schools on the Isle of Man.

senses.definition: To cause (a feeling, state of mind, etc.) to come back or return; to reactivate, to reawaken.
senses.example: Partriche. Of all foules is moſte ſooneſt digeſted: and hath in hym moche nutriment, comforteth the brayne, and maketh ſede of generation,. and reuiueth luſte, whiche is abated.

senses.definition: To renew (something) in one's or people's memories or minds; to bring back (something) to (public) attention; to reawaken.
senses.example: The Harry Potter books and films revived the world’s interest in wizardry.

senses.definition: To make (something which has become faded or unclear) clear or fresh again; to refresh.
senses.example: It was very odd; his clothes were a fine, deep, glossy, black, and yet they looked like the same suit; nay, there were the very darns, with which old acquaintance had made us familiar. […] The truth flashed suddenly upon us—they had been "revived." 'Tis a deceitful liquid that black and blue reviver; we have watched its effects on many a shabby-genteel man. […] [T]he transient dignity of the unhappy man decreased in exact proportion as the "reviver" wore off.

senses.definition: To restore (a metal (especially mercury) or other substance in a compound or mixture) to its pure or unmixed state.
senses.example: to revive a metal after calcination

senses.definition: To give new validity to (a law or legal instrument); to reenact, to revalidate.
senses.example: [Y]et by his moſte excellent witte⸝ he in a few yeres⸝ nat only broughte this realme in good ordre and vnder due obedience⸝ reuiued the lawes⸝ auanced Juſtice⸝ refurniſſhed his dominions⸝ and repayred his manours: […]

senses.definition: To put on a new production of (a musical, play, or other stage performance; also, a film or television programme).
senses.example: A Prologue to the Play of Queene Elizabeth [I] as it vvas laſt revived at the Cock-pit, in vvhich the Author taxeth the moſt corrupted copy novv imprinted, vvhich vvas publiſhed vvithout his conſent.

senses.definition: To bring (someone) back to a state of health or vigour.
senses.example: What helpes reuiue, / the thriuing, to thriue. / Plough fence and ſtore, / aught elſe before.

senses.definition: To rerun (an election).
To recover from a faint; to return to a state of consciousness.
senses.example: He is in ſuche a ſwounde [swoon] yͭ I wene he wyll neuer reuyue againe […]

senses.definition: Of a dead person or animal: to be brought back to life.
senses.example: For Chriſt therfore dyed and roſe agayne⸝ ãd [and] revived⸝ that he ſhuld be lorde both of deed and quicke.

senses.definition: Of a person, animal, or plant: to return to a state of health or vigour, especially after almost dying.
senses.example: I Quycken I reuyue as a thyng dothe that fyrſt doth begyn to ſtyrre or yͭ was wyddered or almoſte deed and retourneth to lyfe againe⸝ […]

senses.definition: To recover from a state of decline, neglect, oblivion, or obscurity; to become active or lively again; to reanimate, to revitalize.
senses.example: Classical learning revived in the 15th century.

senses.definition: Of a feeling, state of mind, etc.: to come back or return; to be reactivated or reawakened.
senses.example: [W]hẽ [when] he ſaw the lord de la vale his hert reuyued and thought there was ſome tretye in hande.

senses.definition: Of a metal (especially mercury) or other substance in a compound or mixture: to return to its pure or unmixed state.
Of a law or legal instrument: to be given new validity.
Of a musical, play, or other stage performance; also, a film or television programme: to have a new production put on.
senses.example: It is not now doubted but plays will revive, and take their usual place in the opinion of persons of wit and merit, notwithstanding their late apostacy^([sic – meaning apostasy]) in favour of dress and sound.

senses.definition: Synonym of revival (“an act of reviving, or a state of being revived (in various senses)”).
senses.example: [F]irst called at Wotton's, the shoemaker's, who tells me the reason of [Henry] Harris's going from Sir W[illia]m Davenant's house, that he grew very proud and demanded £20 for himself extraordinary, more than [Thomas] Betterton, or any body else, upon every new play, and £10 upon every revive; […]
